title: The phone-call envelope
kid: On a dial-up call your parcels travel in a phone-call envelope. Only your computer and the internet company’s modem open it; the telephone exchange in between just passes the sound along. Before any parcel goes, the two ends say hello: they agree how to talk, check who you are, and give your computer its address.
nerd: PPP (RFC 1661) in HDLC-like framing (RFC 1662): 0x7E flags, address 0xFF and control 0x03 (often compressed away by LCP), a protocol number (0x0021 for IPv4) and a frame check. LCP opens the link and agrees MRU and options, CHAP authenticates with a challenge and a hash (PAP, also common in 1995, just sent the password), and IPCP assigns the address. Then IPv4 packets ride in the frames until someone hangs up.

describe.kid: Your computer and the internet company’s modem sit at the two ends of a phone line, with an envelope going back and forth. One card takes the envelope apart: start, address, what’s inside, your parcel, a check and end. The other card shows the hello: how to talk, who are you, and which address you get.
describe.nerd: The two PPP endpoints sit at the ends of the call while a frame shuttles between them. One card lists the frame: flag 7E, address FF and control 03, protocol 0021, the IP packet, FCS and flag. The other plays LCP configure, CHAP challenge and response, and IPCP handing out 203.0.113.7.

answer.kid: It’s me, here’s my secret sum

hdlc.title: The rented line’s envelope
hdlc.kid: On a rented line between two internet companies, your parcel travels in a plain envelope: where it starts, what’s inside, a check, where it ends. There’s no logging in: the line is theirs all the time. Every ten seconds each router calls “still there?” so they notice at once if the line breaks.
hdlc.nerd: Cisco HDLC, the default on Cisco serial ports: 0x7E flags, address 0x0F (unicast), control 0x00, a two-byte EtherType (0x0800 for IPv4), the packet and a 16-bit FCS. No authentication or negotiation: SLARP keepalives every 10 s carry sequence numbers both ways, and three missed ones take the line protocol down.

describe.kid: Two routers sit at the ends of a rented line, with an envelope going back and forth. One card takes the envelope apart: start, address, what’s inside, your parcel, a check and end. The other card shows the routers checking on each other, and a parcel going across.
describe.nerd: Two routers at the ends of a leased line exchange Cisco HDLC frames. One card lists the frame: flag 7E, address 0F and control 00, type 0800, the IP packet, FCS and flag. The other plays SLARP keepalives each way with their sequence numbers, then an IP packet.
